chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Idrees ibn Zayd, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We have uncultivated lands (diya'), and they have boundaries, and therein are pastures. And for a man from us there are sheep and camels, and he needs those pastures for his camels and his sheep. Is it permissible for him to reserve (hima) the pasture for his need of it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the land is his land, then it is permissible for him to reserve it and dedicate it to what he needs it for.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I said to him, 'The man sells the pasture?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the land is his land, then there is no problem.'

key_terms.يَحْمِيَ: To reserve or enclose (specifically for livestock)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for reselling or reserving pasture land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the private ownership rights (milkiyyah) of pasture lands, affirming that an individual may designate them as a protected grazing area (hima) for their livestock or sell them outright. It reflects the early Shia juristic consensus that clear ownership grants the proprietor full discretion over the land's utility and disposition, distinguishing private property from communal or public domains.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Idrees Bin Zayd, 
from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There is a place for us and for it are boundaries, and therein is a pasture field, and for the man from us there as sheep, and camels, and he is needy to that pasture for his camels and his sheep. Is it Permissible for him that he reserves the pasture for his needs to it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the land was his land, so it would be for him to reserve and that would come to be for what he needs it for’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man sells the pasture?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the land was his land, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Idris ibn Zayd who has said the following: “Regarding my question before abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, - after saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, we have a property that has boundaries and a pasture - about a man from us who has sheep and camel. He needs those pastures for his camel and sheep if it is permissible for him to preserve and protect the pastures for his needs.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If the land is his land he has the right to reserve and keep it for his needs.’ I then asked, ‘Can the man sell the pastures?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If the land is his land, it is not unlawful to do so.’”
